title: Ultrasound Assessment of an Isolated Rupture of the Medial Bundle of a Bifid Distal Biceps Tendon - PMC

PMC Copyright notice PMCID: PMC10802860  PMID: 38264605 Abstract This case study describes a patient with a clinically ruptured distal biceps tendon, with ultrasound detecting an isolated rupture of the medial bundle of a bifid distal biceps tendon. figures.caption: Figure 1. Open in a new tab Longitudinal ultrasound image of the distal biceps tendon showing a corrugated appearance (arrow) with fluid and hematoma in the paratenon (asterisk). Br: Brachialis muscle

Figure 2. Open in a new tab Transverse ultrasound image of an abnormally thickened ruptured distal biceps tendon (white arrow) surrounded by fluid and hematoma (asterisk), with an intact bicipital aponeurosis (blue arrow). A: Brachial artery

Figure 3. Open in a new tab Longitudinal ultrasound image of the corrugated distal biceps tendon at the insertion, demonstrating a rounded tendon stump (arrow) with only fluid and hematoma at the radial tuberosity (asterisk). RT: Radial tuberosity

Figure 4. Open in a new tab Transverse ultrasound image of the distal biceps tendon. Thickened and ruptured distal biceps tendon (white arrow) with surrounding hematoma (asterisk). Intact accessory distal biceps tendon (red arrow) could be identified separately, with movement on dynamic forearm supination and pronation

Figure 5. Open in a new tab Longitudinal ultrasound image of the intact long head component of the bifid distal biceps tendon (red arrow) demonstrating a normal thin uniform linear hyperechoic tendon. Br: Brachialis muscle

Figure 6. Open in a new tab Transverse ultrasound image of the musculotendinous junction (blue arrow) demonstrating the short head component (white arrow) and long head component (red arrow) as two distinct structures. The short head component (white arrow) was the ruptured element of the bifid distal biceps tendon. Br: Brachialis muscle, A: Brachial artery
